reasoning: Read test/test_ducklib.py:1634-1648 directly. test_create_array_value builds a 3-element INTEGER array value via duckdb_create_array_value, asserts only `av != 0`, then destroys av/v1/v2/v3/int_type -- it never reads back the array's length or element contents. This is a real, precisely-located gap: the sibling container-value tests do verify contents -- test_create_get_list_value (1531-1550) asserts duckdb_get_list_size == 2 and duckdb_get_list_child(...) == 10/20; test_create_get_map_value (1563-1599) asserts duckdb_get_map_size/key/value; test_create_get_struct_value (1602-1631) asserts duckdb_get_struct_child == 42/99. test_create_array_value has no analogous readback, and no other test in the file exercises the contents of a value built by duckdb_create_array_value (verified via grep across the file; the only other array-related tests -- test_create_array_type at 1791, duckdb_array_type_array_size/child_type -- exercise the LOGICAL TYPE constructor, not a create_array_value VALUE). aux_destroy_value (1165-1170) performs no validation either, so nothing in the test indirectly confirms element values. Checked duckdb.h (v1.3.2-era C API, matching the pin duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6): unlike duckdb_get_list_size/duckdb_get_list_child and duckdb_get_struct_child/duckdb_get_map_size/key/value, there is no dedicated duckdb_get_array_size/duckdb_get_array_child getter for a duckdb_value of ARRAY type -- so the reviewer's specific suggested fix (mirror the list/map/struct getter pattern) isn't literally available as a 1:1 API call, but the underlying defect claim (contents never read back) is independently true regardless of which readback mechanism would be used (e.g. duckdb_value_to_string(av) and asserting on the rendered '[1, 2, 3]' text, or a SQL round-trip, both remain viable and are also unused). This mirrors the already-accepted pattern in TST-cover-6 (weak assertion on a create/get pair) and is a pure test-coverage gap, not a library bug -- consistent with the low severity assigned. No evidence found that the gap is covered elsewhere or that verification is otherwise infeasible, so I confirm at the claimed severity.
